Actor.description:
Who is acting, as the server established it. `session` = a verified Supabase session
(the web apps' transport); the key audiences come from `infrx.auth`.
Actor.title: Actor

Availability.description:
A feature's availability as FastAPI states it. A failed fetch is `unknown` with a
reason; it is never rendered as a zero count or a disabled feature.
Availability.title: Availability

Credits.description:
The individual's CREDIT wallet. No wallet yet is `wallet_id: null` with zero figures (the
database's own answer); `spent` is null when it cannot be computed exactly.
Credits.title: Credits

KeySummary.description: Never the secret or its hash.
KeySummary.title: KeySummary

LegacyStatement.description: Historical USD, its own unit, never summed with CREDIT (R72).
LegacyStatement.title: LegacyStatement

RequestSummary.description:
One owned request. Execution (`state`) and settlement (`settlement_state`) are separate
fields; money is in the request's own unit; `result_access` is F2C.b's read outcome over the
persisted fields (the database's clock decides available vs expired).
RequestSummary.title: RequestSummary

Session.description: A signed-in session, for Next to set as its cookies. Never in a URL or a log.
Session.title: Session

UnknownUsage.description: A request whose usage is unknown: the hold is quarantined, never charged.
UnknownUsage.title: UnknownUsage

ApiKeyAuth.description: A consumer or provider-dev API key (`/v1/*`).

CheckpointSignature.description: HMAC of the raw body by a LAB_CHECKPOINT_KEYS key.
CheckpointSignature.name: X-Infrx-Signature

SessionBearer.description: The signed-in user's Supabase session, forwarded by the web app's server; verified by the auth server.

get.description:
Readiness for the host itself: component state for a direct loopback peer (I2B's
`deploy/lib.sh wait_ready` polls it unauthenticated), the unknown-path answer for
anyone else. A request relayed by the edge carries a proxy header, so it is refused
here even if the edge rule that 404s `/readyz` were lost (observe/route.py's rule).

post.description:
The chat body, always async. A `Prefer` header here is ignored - the route is the
preference - so none is reported applied. A streaming body is refused as what the
client sent (`param="stream"`), never as a `Prefer` it did not send (review N3).
